summary: Split off MPI-427: the mirror is infra (an approval-gated Cloudflare change), not an app bug.

Origin decided: a second Cloudflare custom domain on cubric-models (Fabio, approval-gated). The reporting user is unreachable, so the mirror ships UNPROVEN against his DPI - it defeats hostname-keyed blocking only. Off-Cloudflare fallbacks costed: GitHub Releases is dead on arrival (36 of 96 R2-hosted deps exceed its 2GB per-asset cap, up to 41GB), Hugging Face is the fallback and needs a path rewrite in _mirrorUrlsFor. Starting the one piece not blocked on Fabio: the failover retry has never executed and has no test.

Approach pivoted to Hugging Face and written up as a 4-phase plan in checklist.md. Cloudflare second-hostname dropped: cubric.studio is young and uncategorised, so a category filter blocks the DOMAIN and a second subdomain does not dodge it; madponyinteractive.com fails the same test. HF beats FQDN, domain and provider keying. R2 stays primary - the Xet throttle that MPI-129/140 fixed is MULTI-CONNECTION, aria2c is Pod-only, and the local path is single-stream DownloaderHelper, so an HF mirror in downloadManager.js is local-only by construction and cannot regress Pod speed. Phase 1 blocks the rest: classify 97 deps / 400.8 GB by comparing our recorded sha256 to each upstream HF LFS pointer oid, because a mirror serving non-identical bytes fails the post-download verify. Its re-host total decides HF free (best-effort, not a plannable quota) vs PRO (10 TB).

Handoff a2ec6609 created. Phases 1 and 1.5 done: 97 deps classified by sha256 (32 deps / 37.8 GB to upload, the rest verified byte-identical elsewhere), CivitAI licences swept with the badge method, credit blocks added for coyotte and S1LV3RC01N, three licence docs written. Next session starts at phase 2, the HF upload. Free tier confirmed correct - 8.7 TB quota, do not buy PRO.

Mirror failover SHIPPED and validated. All 97 R2-hosted deps now have a second download origin on Hugging Face, 97/97 HEAD-verified byte-identical against their recorded sha256, and an end-to-end run against a dead origin completed off huggingface.co and passed the SHA256 verify using the shipped default with no env override. 31 of our own bakes were re-hosted (37.8 GB, bandwidth-capped at 3 MiB/s so the machine stayed usable); 66 were already byte-identical upstream and only needed a per-dep mirrorUrl. Three defects surfaced that the plan did not predict: mirrors were derived from the MUTATED depJob.url so a prefixed mirror double-prefixed the second hop and broke the walk; a mirror that 404s overwrote the blocked user's VPN remedy with 'status code 404', making the failover worse than none; and the engine archive plus custom-node zips share FileDownloader from github.com and would have been rewritten onto a 404. The resume guard was re-keyed from URL pathname onto the dep sha256 - a mirror changes the prefix AND the filename, so a URL test would have deleted exactly the partial failover exists to preserve (MPI-317 re-armed). qwen-lora-headswap, the one dep with no second route, was resolved by Fabio naming Alissonerdx/BFS-Best-Face-Swap (MIT), confirmed by hash. Root cause of that gap - an empty origin field - is now a rule in the add-model playbook, which had called origin 'informational'. NOT proven against the original reporter's transfer-stage DPI; he is unreachable.
